findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` once, when the class body executes at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` therefore gets the same process-start timestamp, not the time the assignment was queued. The field exists to record when the source was queued, so any later use for ordering, staleness checks or logging will see wrong data. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it passes despite this bug.

findings.title: Cycle-breaking is not tested on the deassign path or end-to-end through inbound sync
findings.body: The only new test of the suppression behaviour covers `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with an `AssignmentSource` that matches the integration. Three paths are untested. First, `deassign(..., assignment_source=...)` never has its suppression asserted. Second, `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (the actual webhook entry point that builds the source, for both assign and deassign) is never checked for skipping the outbound call. The existing inbound tests don't assert that `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called. Third, there is no test that a different integration's source still propagates outward, which the `should_sync` comment says is intended. A regression in any of these would reintroduce the sync loop unnoticed.

findings.title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to abstract `sync_status_outbound`
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`. Nothing in this PR passes it, and status sync is not part of the assignee-cycle fix. It widens the contract for all subclasses with an argument that is never populated. This is misleading, and it suggests status sync is cycle-protected when it is not. Either remove it or wire it through.
